properties.P1-serverVerifiableProof: The AGS server verifies a cryptographic proof itself; it does not trust a result reported by the caller.
properties.P2-keyOutsideSameUserReach: The signing key cannot be read or used by a same-user process without a fresh human action for that approval.
properties.P3-trustedDisplay: The human sees the bound runId/taskId/stage/revision/digest on a surface that same-user processes cannot draw or alter.
properties.P4-bindingComplete: The signed statement binds runId, taskId, stageId, assignmentId, approvalRevision, approvalDigest and a server challenge.
properties.P5-singleUse: A server-issued challenge is consumed once in the same transaction that records the approval; reuse, replay and expiry are rejected.
properties.P6-revocation: Key revocation and approval revocation are recorded by the server and checked before any record or effect.
properties.P7-verifierAndTrustAnchorProtected: The verifier code and the enrolled approver key registry cannot be changed by same-user processes.

evidence: No approver app, enrolled approver key registry or approval adapter exists in AGS at the start commit: mcp-server/src/index.ts:68 states neither bundled host exposes a cryptographically distinct direct-human approval event.
The AGS server principal is profileId=ags-local-server, protectedPrincipal=false (docs/implementation-3x/approved-role-source.ko.md:52), so P7 is unmet even if an app were built.

CredUIPromptForWindowsCredentials returns the entered credential to the calling process, and UAC secure desktop consent is an elevation decision delivered to the elevated process; neither yields a proof the AGS server can verify (P1 fails). Documentation analysis only; no probe was run.

UserConsentVerifier.RequestVerificationAsync returns only a UserConsentVerificationResult enum to the calling process. There is no proof the AGS server can verify, and a same-user process can report any value (P1 fails).

KeyCredentialManager keys are non-exportable and RequestSignAsync signs caller-chosen bytes after a Windows Hello gesture. The prompt does not show the approval statement, so a same-user process can obtain a signature over its own statement when the user expects a prompt (P3 fails). Which same-user processes can open a named key for an unpackaged desktop caller was not established (P2 UNKNOWN).
P7 is unmet for the same reason as above.

probe-strings: Claude Code 2.1.283 carries elicitation/create and Elicitation/ElicitationResult hook output schemas that 'programmatically accept or decline' a request and 'override the action or content before the response is sent to the MCP server'.
The response reaching the server carries no attestation, and a configured hook can produce or rewrite it (P1, P2 fail). The AGS server does not call elicitation (mcp-server/src/server.ts:462).

liveObservation.reason: NOT_RUN(비용 승인 대기): a live run needs one model turn. The development lead obtains user cost approval and issues a separate GO.
liveObservation.isolatedCommand: cd <scratch>/empty-cwd && claude --bare -p "call the probe tool once" --setting-sources local --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <scratch>/elicit-probe.mcp.json --max-turns 2 --output-format stream-json (scratch MCP server answers tools/call by sending elicitation/create and logging the raw response; no user config, hook, plugin or MCP registration is changed)
liveObservation.isolation: --bare skips hooks from settings and installed plugins (including AGS hooks), auto-memory and CLAUDE.md auto-discovery while still honoring --mcp-config; --setting-sources local with an empty scratch cwd loads no user or project settings; --strict-mcp-config ignores other MCP servers. --settings alone is not isolation because it only adds settings. --safe-mode is not used because it also disables MCP servers, which may include the probe server. Per claude --help 2.1.283, --bare reads Anthropic auth only from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper (OAuth and keychain are never read), so the run needs an API key the user approves for this cost.
liveObservation.responder: In -p mode no person or terminal UI can answer, and --bare loads no Elicitation hook. Who answers (host auto-cancel or decline, or no response) is UNKNOWN and is what the probe server log must record. Observing a human answer needs an interactive run with the same flags minus -p, and the log must record the raw action and content the server received.
liveObservation.estimatedCost: one short non-interactive turn, on the order of a few thousand tokens; not measured
liveObservation.wouldChangeDetermination: No. Hook override is shown in the pinned binary schema; a live run would confirm delivery shape only.

evidence: probe-strings: codex-cli 0.155.1 carries elicitation/create, McpServerElicitationRequest, the app-server method mcpServer/elicitation/request, ResolveElicitation, an approval config key mcp_elicitations and a guardian path ('guardian MCP elicitation review ... codex_strict_auto_review').

The answer can come from any app-server client and carries no proof the AGS server can verify (P1, P2 fail). The guardian strings limit automated review to mcp_tool_call-kind form elicitations with an empty schema, so guardian review is a narrow additional path, not the main one. forgedSignature.point: intake verifies proof.signature over the JCS statement with the enrolled key

crossRunReuse.point: intake compares every binding field and the challenge nonce, issuedAt and expiresAt with the server's own pending approval request

replay.point: intake consumes the challenge nonce in the same transaction that writes the record

useAfterRevocation.point: R18-a intake and the R18-b current read check approval and key revocation

expiredChallenge.point: intake rejects challenges past expiresAt by server clock

unenrolledOrRevokedKey.point: intake resolves keyId only from the server-held approver registry, requires proof.keyId == statement.approver.keyId and requires enrollmentRevision to equal the registry revision

hookModelPeerEvent.point: intake accepts only a proof envelope; no hook, tool argument or peer message path creates a record

denyRecordedAsApproval.point: intake writes the R17 approval record only for decision=approve; decision=deny consumes the challenge and closes the pending request as denied without a record

trustAnchorTamper.point: needs a protected verifier principal; not satisfiable inside R18-a
